statement: Guardicore continuously discovers assets and flows in real time and builds a living communication map.
Guardicore's map ties connections to processes, providing visualization at App / Environment / Role / Process granularity.
No public evidence found for a specific flow-history retention duration (days).
Guardicore integrates with Tenable to import CVE data and label assets by CVE/risk on the map.
Guardicore's flow telemetry surfaces unrecognized/unmanaged assets and flows via its AI-analyzed dependency map.
Guardicore policies are authored against labels/tags and identity (not IP/VLAN).
Guardicore includes AI-driven policy recommendation and generation.
Guardicore supports policy simulation / dry-run via 'Allow Mode' before enforcement.
No public evidence found describing an instant 1-click rollback capability.
No public evidence found describing hierarchical / inherited rule support.
Guardicore supports a broad range of OSes including Windows Server 2000-2019, RHEL/CentOS/Ubuntu, Solaris SPARC, AIX, and HP-UX.
Guardicore natively secures Kubernetes via CNI-level enforcement with DaemonSet+Helm and covers OpenShift OVN, though the older vendor blog notes OpenShift/Cilium support was still being expanded.
Guardicore offers both agent-based enforcement and agentless visibility via NetFlow/sFlow/IPFIX network collectors.
Guardicore management server can be deployed on-prem or SaaS; explicit certification for air-gapped isolated deployment is not documented.
A cited customer deployment secured 300,000 endpoints in two weeks, exceeding the 50,000-workload threshold.
No public evidence found citing agent CPU % under load.
No public evidence found citing agent RAM footprint in MB.
No public evidence found citing added network latency in ms.
No public evidence found describing agent fail-safe / traffic-continuity behavior on agent crash.
No public evidence found addressing whether agent install/update requires a server reboot.
Guardicore exposes a REST API used by integrations and automation recipes; 100% admin coverage is not verified from public sources.
Guardicore integrates with Splunk and IBM QRadar via CEF/syslog and a Splunkbase add-on for SIEM/SOAR consumption.
Guardicore has a ServiceNow-certified CMDB integration via an app in the ServiceNow Store.
Vendor pages describe REST API and automation recipes for CI/CD DevOps pipelines; specific Jenkins/GitLab/Terraform module coverage is not fully detailed in public sources.
Guardicore enforcement is process-level at Layer 7, tying each connection to the initiating process.
Guardicore includes patented dynamic deception (honeypot redirection) and threat detection.
Guardicore publishes a PCI-DSS mapping whitepaper and aligns with NIST SP 800-207; ISO 27001 and IEC 62443 ready-made reports are not confirmed publicly.
Agent-to-aggregator traffic is encrypted and authenticated on TCP/443 using TLS 1.2 (not TLS 1.3 as required).
No public evidence found describing controller HA cluster architecture (active-active / active-passive).
No public evidence explicitly describing autonomous mode where the agent enforces policy after controller loss.
No public evidence found describing DR site sync / backup procedures.
No public evidence found of FIPS 140-2/140-3 or Common Criteria EAL4+ certification for the Guardicore product.
Guardicore is stated to align with IEC 62443 in an OT integration with NVIDIA BlueField / Siemens, but no formal certification from Siemens/Honeywell/ABB is documented.
